title: Bounded polynomial presentation categories augmented to an arbitrary algebra
statement: Fix an infinite set $I$ as a common bound [def-weil-size-convention], commutative rings $A,B,C$ and maps $A\to B\to C$. Define $\mathcal D_C^+$ with objects $(T,c)$ where $T\subseteq I$ and $c:T\to C$, representing $B[T]\to C$ by evaluation; morphisms are all augmentation-preserving $B$-algebra maps. Define $\mathcal E_C^+$ with objects $(S,T,\beta,c)$, $S,T\subseteq I$, $\beta:A[S]\to B$ an $A$-algebra map, and $c:T\to C$, representing $P=A[S]$, $Q=P[T]$ with its compatible augmentation to $C$. Its morphisms are commuting pairs of $A$-algebra maps preserving both augmentations. The induced base-change map on $B[T]$ is uniquely fixed by its square with coefficient specialization $Q\to B[T]$. Define $u^+:\mathcal E_C^+\to\mathcal D_C^+$ by $(S,T,\beta,c)\mapsto(T,c)$, on morphisms by that canonical base-change map. Thus $u^+$ represents $Q\otimes_P B$ and the opposite categories with the opposite functor give the identity-cover presentation sites for arbitrary $C$, without polynomiality or flatness assumptions.
